newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Gabon increases ex-Paris cargo rates by 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Air Gabon increases ex-Paris cargo rates by 5 pct.

text.p: West African airline, Air Gabon, said it had increased its ex-Paris cargo rates to the Gabonese capital, Libreville and Pointe Noire, in neighbouring Congo, by five percent, effective March 1.
"The increases are in line with those of Air France Cargo, which is the market leader in French-speaking Africa, a Paris-based cargo official for Air Gabon told Reuters.
Air Gabon operates four, weekly Boeing 747 combi flights from Paris to Libreville, each with a cargo capacity of 35 to 40 tonnes.
Weekly stopovers are made at Marseille, Nice, London Gatwick and Rome en route from Paris to Libreville.

"Cargo load factors on the route are good at present and in addition we can now offer our customers palletised capacity from Libreville to onward destinations in West and Central Africa in the form of a Boeing 767 passenger aircraft," the official said.
The 767 replaced a 737 passenger aircraft which could only accomodate bulk freight, the official added.
"Air Gabon will be opening a new route between Libreville and Nairobi later this month using the 767."
Air Gabon's major shipper customers are oil exploration companies. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
